settings.title: Settings
settings.clipboardHintMaster: Copying or revealing a cookie asks for your master password first.
settings.clipboardHintHello: Copying or revealing a cookie asks for Windows Hello first.
settings.moveText: AltDock copies its database to {path} and restarts to use it. The old database is deleted after the restart. Logs and the app's browser data stay in the old folder, so the theme and other view preferences reset.
settings.bandwidthStale: Set to {kbps} kbit/s, but Windows has restarted since: apply it again.
settings.bandwidthHint: Caps outbound (upload) traffic only, for all Roblox clients together, as a Windows QoS policy. Applying needs admin rights (Windows asks each time) and lasts until Windows restarts.
settings.shutdownHintClose: Windows' own shutdown timer. When it runs out, Windows closes every app without asking, so unsaved work elsewhere is lost. AltDock's clients are closed 30 s before (if AltDock hasn't restarted since). Cancel it here, even after a restart of AltDock.
settings.shutdownHint: Windows' own shutdown timer. When it runs out, Windows closes every app without asking, so unsaved work elsewhere is lost. Cancel it here, even after a restart of AltDock.
settings.publicHint: Turned off, AltDock doesn't launch on a network Windows calls Public (café, hotel, school Wi-Fi), and a master-password vault locks there.
settings.publicConfirmText: Others on a public network can see which servers your clients connect to, and can try to reach this PC. With this on, AltDock launches there too. Only turn it on for a network you trust, and turn it off again after.
settings.backgroundCovers: The theme covers {n}% of the picture
settings.encryptionHintMaster: Asked at start and after auto-lock.
settings.encryptionHintDpapi: Windows DPAPI: unlocks with your Windows sign-in, no prompt.
settings.antiAfkHowHint: Only after 5 s without keyboard or mouse input: each client is brought to the front for a moment (a minimized one is restored, then minimized again), gets an F13 press (no game uses it, so the character stays put) and the window you had in front comes back. Roblox only counts a real key press in the window in front.
settings.publicNotNow: Not on a public network now.
settings.importWrongPassword: Wrong password, or the file is damaged.
settings.robloxMissing: Roblox isn't installed. Install it here or from roblox.com.
settings.openLogsHint: AltDock's own logs, for a bug report
settings.languageHint: Windows follows the Windows display language when AltDock has it, else English.
settings.accentHint: Buttons, switches and highlights. Pick a preset or any colour.
settings.densityHint: Row height in the accounts list.
settings.discordHint: Your Discord profile shows “Playing AltDock” with the game and how many alts run. Only while Discord is open on this PC.
settings.closeToTrayHint: The window hides; running clients and auto-rejoin keep working.
settings.skipSplashHint: Opens AltDock right away, without the start-up animation. Applies from the next start.
settings.multiHint: AltDock holds Roblox's single-instance lock while it runs, so each account gets its own client. Turn it on before the first client starts.
settings.protectLoginHint: While AltDock's clients run, lock Roblox's shared sign-in files so clients can't overwrite each other's session (error 773, wrong account in game). Meanwhile Roblox's own app can't save its sign-in.
settings.launchDelayHint: Wait between two launches when several accounts launch at once. About a second either way is added.
settings.minimizeHint: Each client is minimized once, when it first reaches a game, without taking the focus; full-quality accounts stay visible. Home shows its last picture. Anti-AFK in focus mode skips minimized clients, so use In the background.
settings.autoRejoinHint: Relaunch a client Roblox disconnects (kicked, server shut down, connection lost) into the same target.
settings.autoRestartHint: Relaunch a client that closes without AltDock closing it, or whose window stops responding for 30 s. Closing Roblox's window yourself looks the same, so close clients from AltDock.
settings.antiAfkHint: So Roblox doesn't disconnect idle clients after 20 minutes, each client in a game gets a key press. A client can opt out under its limits on Home.
settings.antiAfkEveryHint: Roblox disconnects after 20 idle minutes, so 1 to 19.
settings.breakerHint: Rejoins and restarts of one account within this time. Each waits twice as long as the one before (at most a minute); past the limit AltDock leaves it and tells you.
settings.closeGraceHint: How long a client AltDock closes gets to close by itself before it is ended.
settings.launchArgsHint: Extra words for every client, after its launch link (for a bootstrapper, say). No quotes or & | < > ^. An account can have its own in its details.
settings.fpsCapHint: The frame rate each client AltDock starts is capped at, unless the account has its own. AltDock sets Roblox's own Maximum Frame Rate just before the client starts and puts yours back once the client has read it; a batch does so for each launch. Off leaves Roblox alone.
settings.lowGraphicsHint: Clients AltDock starts use Roblox's lowest graphics quality, which saves a lot of GPU and CPU with many clients. Your own Roblox graphics setting is put back right after, and again when such a client closes (or, if AltDock isn't running then, when it next starts).
settings.autoUpdateHint: When Roblox has a new version and no Roblox client runs (nor a launch or batch), install it. The installer is checked to be signed by Roblox Corporation first. Never over a bootstrapper such as Bloxstrap, which updates Roblox itself.
settings.memRestartHint: Close and relaunch a client whose commit size stays over this for 30 s, into the same game, within the restart limit in Settings, Launching. Not during a batch. It disconnects the client, but it's the only way to free its private memory.
settings.memThrottleHint: While a client's commit size is over this, hold it to the CPU limit below, which lowers its frame rate. Lifted once it is back under 90 %. Tightens a client's own limit, never loosens it.
settings.trimHint: Ask Windows to page each client's memory out on a schedule, and sooner if it grows; it comes back as used. A client's own limit on Home wins.
settings.spreadHint: Give each client its own share of the cores, round-robin. Cores picked for a client on Home win. Skipped when there are too few cores for two per client.
settings.adaptiveHint: Clients whose window isn't in front get the limits below; the one you're playing runs free. A limit set on one client wins over these.
settings.adaptiveBgHint: CPU limit (a share of all cores), efficiency mode and how often to trim memory, for clients not in front.
settings.fairCapHint: Divides the CPU among the clients, so each gets a smaller cap as more run. The client in front, clients loading or not responding and Full quality accounts run free. A client's own limit on Home wins.
settings.panicHint: Works from any app, even a game in front: stops every Roblox client at once, like the Hold to stop all button. Modifiers and one key, like Ctrl+Shift+F12. Empty turns it off.
settings.cleanLogsHint: Delete Roblox's client logs over a day old or over 50 MB, at start and every hour. A running client's log is kept.
settings.masterPasswordHint: Changing it only re-wraps the key; cookies are not re-encrypted.
settings.autoLockHint: Locks the vault and wipes the key from memory.
settings.clipboard: Clear clipboard after copying a cookie
settings.cacheHint: How long the info panel reuses what Roblox said before asking again. Presence refreshes every minute while Accounts is open.
settings.backupHint: One password-protected .altdock file with every account, its cookie and its groups.
settings.aboutHint: AltDock talks to roblox.com (and Roblox's DevForum and newsroom for News) and to Discord once you set a webhook, and changes nothing on your PC unless you apply a bandwidth limit. It sends nothing to RoALT: no update checks, no online counter.
settings.setMasterText: AltDock will ask for it at start and after auto-lock.
settings.changeMasterText: Enter the current password, then the new one.
settings.removeMasterText: Cookies will be protected by your Windows account instead and open without a prompt.
settings.removeMasterDone: Master password removed. The vault now opens with Windows.
settings.exportText: The file holds every cookie, encrypted with this password. You need it to import the file.
settings.moveDialog: Choose a folder for AltDock's data
settings.selfUpdateHint: Asks GitHub Releases at start and every 6 hours. A new version is offered, never installed without your click, and its installer runs only if it carries AltDock's release signature.
settings.onlineCount: Show how many people use AltDock
settings.onlineCountHint: Every 2 minutes, sends AltDock's counter a random ID made when AltDock starts and how many Roblox clients AltDock is running, and nothing else. The counts show beside the Discord button. Off: nothing is sent.
settings.clientInstallHint: Downloads Roblox's installer from setup.rbxcdn.com and runs it once it is verified as signed by Roblox Corporation
settings.backgroundHint: Your own picture behind the app (PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, up to 8 MB). It is kept in AltDock's data.

settings.publicBannerBlocked: Public network: launching is off until you join a private network.
settings.updateConfirmText_one: AltDock closes while it updates and starts again by itself. {count} Roblox client keeps running, and the restarted AltDock follows it again. Its CPU limits are lifted for the few seconds AltDock is closed.
settings.updateConfirmText_other: AltDock closes while it updates and starts again by itself. {count} Roblox clients keep running, and the restarted AltDock follows them again. Their CPU limits are lifted for the few seconds AltDock is closed.

launch.limits.help: The limit is a share of all CPU cores; its frame rate drops with it. For a fixed frame rate, use the FPS cap when launching. Efficiency mode lowers its priority, as Task Manager does. Trimming asks Windows to page its memory out; it comes back as used. Limits set here win over the adaptive manager's. Anti-AFK briefly brings this client to the front for a Space press while you're away; it skips a minimized client.

launch.running.closeAllText_other: {count} Roblox clients AltDock started will close. Unsaved progress in those games is lost.
launch.kill.hint: Hold for a second: ends every Roblox client at once, without saving
launch.multi.turnOnText: Roblox says it doesn't officially support running several clients at once. AltDock only holds the name Roblox's client checks when it starts and never touches the client itself, which Roblox says its enforcement against modified clients doesn't cover. Roblox has broken multi-instance before and may again.
launch.multi.closeText_one: Every running Roblox client closes ({count} process), including ones AltDock didn't start. Unsaved progress in those games is lost.
launch.multi.closeText_other: Every running Roblox client closes ({count} processes), including ones AltDock didn't start. Unsaved progress in those games is lost.
launch.multi.takeOverTitle: Take over from the running Roblox?
launch.multi.takeOverText_one: AltDock closes Roblox's own "already running" marker inside the running client ({count} process) with a standard Windows call, so new clients can start next to it without closing it. Nothing in the client's memory is changed, but this reaches into a running Roblox: if a client misbehaves afterwards, close Roblox instead. Roblox's anti-cheat may see the access.
launch.multi.takeOverText_other: AltDock closes Roblox's own "already running" marker inside the running clients ({count} processes) with a standard Windows call, so new clients can start next to it without closing it. Nothing in the client's memory is changed, but this reaches into a running Roblox: if a client misbehaves afterwards, close Roblox instead. Roblox's anti-cheat may see the access.

discord.intro: Get told in a Discord channel when a client crashes, gets disconnected or is relaunched. AltDock posts to a webhook you create in the channel's settings (Integrations, Webhooks). Discord is the only place besides Roblox AltDock sends anything to, and only once a webhook is set. Messages name accounts by display name and username; never a cookie, link or log.

discord.notSet: Not set. Paste the webhook URL Discord shows (Copy Webhook URL).

vault.recovery.showText: It is shown only this once. If you forget your master password, it lets you set a new one. It works once, and then you get a new code.
vault.recovery.copied: Copied. The clipboard clears itself shortly.
vault.recovery.limitFile: A code file on this PC opens your vault for anyone who finds it. Keep it on a USB stick, a phone or paper.
vault.recovery.limitPc: It works only for this Windows user on this PC. After a Windows reinstall or on a new PC it won't help; a .altdock backup does.
vault.recovery.forgotText: Enter your recovery code and choose a new master password. The code then stops working and you get a new one.
vault.recovery.rowHintOn: A code is set. Replacing it stops the old one working.
vault.recovery.rowHintOff: Optional. A code lets you set a new master password if you forget this one.
vault.recovery.offerText: Optional. If you forget the master password, this code lets you set a new one. Without it, the vault can't be opened.
vault.recovery.replaceText: Enter your master password. The old code stops working straight away.
vault.recovery.createText: Enter your master password. The code is shown only once.
vault.recovery.changeReminder: Your recovery code keeps working after this. If someone else may know the old password, replace the code too.

performance.bench.needGame: Start a client and let it reach a game first.
performance.bench.measuring: Measuring… keep your clients in their games.

performance.bench.none: Nothing to change: your settings already fit.
performance.bench.stale: Your settings changed since this measurement. Measure again for suggestions that fit them.

performance.bench.why.fpsCapGpu: Your GPU peaked at {gpu}%, so the cap is a step lower: {fps} FPS.
performance.bench.why.lowGraphics: Your PC is busy with this many clients: the lowest graphics save GPU and CPU.
performance.bench.why.lowGraphicsGpu: Your GPU peaked at {gpu}%: the lowest graphics save most of that.
performance.bench.why.lighterRendering: Lighter graphics flags use much less GPU memory.
performance.bench.why.minimizeOnLaunch: With {n} clients, minimized ones save GPU while you play one.
performance.bench.why.tinyOnLaunch: Tiny {width}×{height} windows draw far fewer pixels, and hidden clients stop drawing.
performance.bench.why.muteOnLaunch: Sound from {n} clients at once is only noise.

performance.bench.why.fairCap: The CPU would be over the limit: each background client gets at most {cap}%.
performance.bench.why.adaptive: Background clients are held to {cap}% CPU, with efficiency mode.
performance.bench.why.adaptiveEco: Windows refused CPU caps here, so background clients get efficiency mode only.
performance.bench.why.trimEveryMin: Frees each client's unused memory every {min} minutes.
performance.bench.why.memThrottle: Clients peaked at {peak} MB: one past {mb} MB is slowed down before it fills your RAM.
performance.bench.why.memRestart: The clients would need more RAM than you have: one past {mb} MB is restarted. A restart disconnects it.
performance.bench.why.memRestartCrash: Long runs crashed {crashes} times this week: a client past {mb} MB is restarted first. A restart disconnects it.
performance.bench.why.previewFps: Home's previews at {fps} FPS leave more for the clients.

settings.multiShort: One client per account, side by side.
settings.launchArgsShort: Extra words after each launch link.
settings.autoRestartShort: Relaunches a client that crashes or hangs.
settings.antiAfkShort: Keeps idle clients from being kicked.
settings.panicShort: Stops every client, from any app.
settings.shutdownShort: Windows' own timer. It closes every app.
settings.publicShort: Off: no launching on Public networks.
settings.aboutShort: What AltDock connects to, and what it changes.
settings.encryptionMoreMaster: Cookies are sealed with AES-256-GCM, using a key made from your master password with Argon2id. Copying or revealing a cookie asks for that password first.
launch.layoutPreviewHint: Shows on your screen, for a few seconds, where each picked account's window will go and in what order

settings.motionHintOn: Liquid motion: pills flow, pages pour in, controls stretch. Kept on this PC.

settings.motionHintOff: No animation at all: everything changes at once.
sessions.lead: Clients here run in hidden Windows sessions of their own, so anti-AFK and macros never take your mouse, keyboard or focus.
sessions.empty: No sessions yet. Add one to run clients in the background.
sessions.health.title: Setup check
sessions.health.lead: Background sessions need RDP Wrapper and a few Windows settings. Set up asks for administrator rights once and fixes everything it can; RDP Wrapper itself you install by following its instructions.
sessions.health.firewallNote: While AltDock's sessions are set up, Remote Desktop from other computers is blocked: only this PC connects to it. “Remove from this PC” lifts the block.
sessions.health.fixRestart: Restart Windows (or the Remote Desktop service), then check again.
sessions.health.setupFailed_one: Setup finished, but {count} step failed: {steps}. The log has the details.
sessions.health.setupFailed_other: Setup finished, but {count} steps failed: {steps}. The log has the details.
sessions.uninstall.title: Remove from this PC
sessions.uninstall.lead: Undoes everything Set up changed on this PC, after one administrator prompt.
sessions.uninstall.dialogTitle: Remove AltDock's sessions from this PC?
sessions.uninstall.text: After one administrator prompt, AltDock removes:
sessions.uninstall.itemFirewall: The firewall rule that blocks Remote Desktop from other computers
sessions.uninstall.itemSettings: The Remote Desktop, graphics and sign-in settings Set up changed, put back as they were
sessions.uninstall.itemProgram: The autostart in sessions and the program copy in ProgramData
sessions.uninstall.itemCertificate: The certificate that signs the session files, and Windows' trust in it
sessions.uninstall.itemSessions: Every session in this list, with its saved sign-in and .rdp file
sessions.uninstall.keeps: Your accounts, macros and RDP Wrapper stay. Log every session off first.
sessions.uninstall.deleteUsers: Also delete the sessions' Windows users and their profiles
sessions.uninstall.deleteUsersHint: Their profile folders go too, with the Roblox installs and everything else in them. Unticked, the users stay and show on the sign-in screen again.
sessions.uninstall.done: AltDock's sessions were removed from this PC.
sessions.uninstall.failed_one: Removed, but {count} step failed: {steps}. The log has the details.
sessions.uninstall.failed_other: Removed, but {count} steps failed: {steps}. The log has the details.
sessions.mode.sharedHint: Several clients under one Windows user, without macros; anti-AFK takes turns between them.
sessions.mode.dedicatedHint: One client under its own Windows user, for a client running a continuous macro.

sessions.noClients: No clients run in this session. Launch some above.

sessions.launch.noAccounts: No accounts in this session. Edit it to add some.

sessions.dialog.accountsHint: The accounts that launch here. Push accounts copies them into the session.

sessions.dialog.added: Added {name}. Run Set up to create its Windows user.

sessions.remove.deleteUserHint: Its profile folder goes too, with the Roblox install and everything else in it.
macros.intro: Run your own AutoHotkey scripts on your clients: from here, from a client's menu on Home, with a hotkey, or when a client reaches a game. Each client gets its own AutoHotkey, told only its window id and process id (A_Args); never a cookie or account.
macros.warning: A macro runs with your full Windows rights, and some games' rules forbid macros: using them is your responsibility. Roblox only reacts to keys sent to the window in front, so a macro brings its own client to the front (WinActivate) before it presses keys (Send), and clients running macros take turns with the focus.
macros.ahkMissing: Not found. Install AutoHotkey v2 to use macros, or pick its AutoHotkey64.exe.
macros.none: No macros yet. Make one, or import a .ahk file.
macros.removeText: It stops wherever it runs. Export it first to keep a copy.
macros.imported: Imported. Review each macro before it can run.
macros.name: Name
macros.hotkeyHint: Starts or stops it on every client in a game, from any app. Modifiers and one key, like Ctrl+Shift+F1. Empty for none.
macros.scriptHint: AutoHotkey v2. Tab types a tab; Shift+Tab leaves the box.
macros.noClients: No client is in a game.
macros.reviewWarn: This macro came from a file or a backup. Once trusted it runs with your full Windows rights: it can read and change your files, AltDock's data included. Trust it only if you understand every line.
macros.discardText: What you changed in this macro isn't saved yet.
macros.lead: Your AutoHotkey v2 scripts, run on each client.
macros.warningShort: Macros run with your full Windows rights.
macros.autorunHint: Starts by itself when this account's client reaches a game
macros.manualHint: Assigned; starts only by hand or with its hotkey
macros.assignHint: Each account runs one macro: ticking an account here takes it off the macro it had.
